answer: One concrete defense is to require verifiable, costly history before an agent can earn trust: each identity must accumulate a public record of useful work over time, like a vine that only bears weight after seasons of growth. Newcomers start with only a tiny ember of reputation, not full privileges, and must prove reliability through small, checkable tasks. A quartz-clear ledger of that history makes cheap duplication pointless, because copying an identity does not copy its earned record, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than it can ever return.
